subject: Operational tolerance proposal and monthly remedy alignment
messages:
From: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@finosys.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@bluestone.com
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Temporary capacity variance + monthly remedy question

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited to proceed. Two items came up in our procurement review that I wanted to surface before we move to signature:

1) We have a fortnightly batch window (3–6AM PT) that will cause short bursts of sustained concurrency during the first 60 days of production. That pattern could produce a small number of transient availability events that are operational (not code) related.

2) Procurement asked whether Redwood would consider a temporary tolerance on the standard uptime commitment (we understand your baseline is in the high 99s) for this onboarding period, in exchange for a clarified, capped monthly remedy (so we avoid open-ended credits during the ramp).

Can you share how you typically handle a temporary exception like this and whether there is a standard cap you’d put on monthly service credits during a ramp? I can attach the batch schedule and our traffic export if that helps.

Appreciate a quick outline so I can explain to procurement.

Best,
Alicia
Alicia Gomez
Head of Platform Ops 
FinoSys

Attachments referenced: batch-window.csv (we'll send if needed)
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@finosys.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Temporary capacity variance + monthly remedy question

Hi Alicia — thanks for the clear note and the context.

Short answer: yes — we have an established playbook for short-term onboarding tolerances and a paired, capped remedy to keep commercial exposure bounded. High-level proposal below; attaching a redline of our standard SLA with the temporary exception called out.

- Window: 60-day temporary exception tied to your onboarding batch cadence (you provided times; we'll align our monitoring hooks).
- Availability baseline: standard is 99.8% (monthly). For the 60 days we can allow a temporary lower bound of 99.0% specifically scoped to the batch windows and ramp-related incidents (not affecting regional, cross-tenant outages).
- Remedy cap: a fixed monthly cap equal to 8% of the monthly invoice for the duration of the exception (not cumulative).
- One-time onboarding concession: a single operational credit (applied to first invoice) to cover runbook sync and extra SRE support.
- Guardrails: (a) incidents attributed to customer misconfiguration are excluded; (b) maintenance windows we schedule together will be carved out; (c) we require access to the batch schedule and a small set of telemetry during the 60 days.

Next steps: Laura and Markus are looped for the legal/ops guardrails. If that all looks reasonable, we can send a short amendment and a DocuSign link to get the exception formalized alongside the Master Services Agreement.

Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0197

Attachment: SLA_redline_JB_v1.pdf
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 12:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Temporary capacity variance + monthly remedy question -- internal notes

Jordan / Markus — quick internal take before we finalize language for Alicia: 

1) 99.0% for two months is reasonable if we narrow scope to the declared batch windows and explicitly exclude platform-level incidents (regional outages, control-plane failures).

2) Remedy cap: suggest we soften to a rounding of 10% of monthly invoice OR $25k, whichever is lower, to avoid extreme exposure on very large invoices. That gives a clear ceiling for procurement.

3) Required evidence: for any claimed event during the band, customer must provide timestamps and a brief post-incident note; Redwood will correlate with our KPIs and provide a remediation decision within 5 business days.

4) Automatic rollback: after 60 days the exception expires unless both parties agree to extend. We should add a clause for a single 30-day extension on mutual agreement.

5) Ops ask (Markus): we need the batch schedule + a small read-only metrics feed (token throughput and queue depth) to tune autoscaling and to rule out customer-side queuing. If customer won't provide telemetry, we should revert to the standard baseline.

I'll draft a one-page amendment that captures the tolerance band, remedy cap ceiling, evidence requirements, and extension mechanics. Jordan — let me know if you want me to include the $25k fixed cap language.

Laura Bennett
Head of Contracts | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@finosys.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Temporary capacity variance + monthly remedy question

Hi Alicia — following internal review, here is a concise, operational proposal you can take to procurement: 

1) Duration: 60 days from production cutover (automatic expiry unless both parties agree to extend once for +30 days).

2) Scoped tolerance: Redwood will temporarily accept a scoped availability tolerance for incidents that occur within the mutually-declared batch windows (3–6AM PT) during onboarding. This does not apply to platform/regional outages or control-plane incidents.

3) Availability threshold during tolerance: 99.0% (monthly) attributable to the scoped batch windows only.

4) Remedy cap: maximum monthly credit equal to the lesser of 8% of the monthly invoice OR $25,000. Credits will be applied to the following invoice cycle.

5) Evidence & coordination: FinoSys will share batch schedule and a read-only telemetry export (token throughput + queue depth) for the 60-day period. For any disputed incident we will correlate logs and provide a remediation decision within 5 business days.

6) Onboarding concession: Redwood will apply a one-time operational credit (listed in the attached onboarding-credit-memo.pdf) to the first invoice for extra SRE support during ramp.

If that aligns with procurement appetite I'll send a short amendment and a DocuSign link to attach to the MSA. Happy to hop on a 15-minute call if procurement wants to walk through the guardrails.

Best,
Jordan
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0197

Attachments: requested-ops-data.csv (customer-sent), SLA_redline_JB_v1.pdf, onboarding-credit-memo.pdf
